pr_title: Mark volume mount as uncertain in case of volume expansion fails
pr_body:
should mark volume mount in actual state even if volume expansion fails so that
reconciler can tear down the volume when needed. To avoid pods start
using it, mark volume as uncertain instead of mounted.

Will add unit test after the logic is reviewed.

Change-Id: I5aebfa11ec93235a87af8f17bea7f7b1570b603d

issue_context.title: UnmapDevice failed for volume X (on node Y : The device Z is still referenced from other Pods)
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
A transient API server outage and/or node authorization failure coupled with pod deletion while block volumes were getting attached/mounted results in block volumes not getting detached properly; thus, delaying the start of a new replica pod on a different node by 6 minutes. 

This is probably a case of Murphy's law where a transient API server access failure and a pod deletion while volumes were getting mounted resulted in an extended outage for a deployment. The problem happened with raw block GCP PDs in GKE, but it can happen with block PVs in any setup.

The prerequisite for this problem is some kind of API server access problem after updating the global map path:
```
2021-02-25T15:17:17+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:17.951191    2126 attacher.go:270] Successfully found attached GCE PD "gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26".
2021-02-25T15:17:17+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:17.951249    2126 operation_generator.go:960] MapVolume.WaitForAttach succeeded for volume "pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26") pod "test-c3406d09-3573-418e-bd71-72a874e5d855-7d4cc6b88b-tlkh6" (UID: "c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10") DevicePath "/dev/disk/by-id/google-gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26"
2021-02-25T15:17:17+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:17.957998    2126 mount_linux.go:178] Detected OS with systemd
2021-02-25T15:17:17+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:17.998592    2126 operation_generator.go:1065] MapVolume.MapPodDevice succeeded for volume "pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26") pod "test-c3406d09-3573-418e-bd71-72a874e5d855-7d4cc6b88b-tlkh6" (UID: "c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10") volumeMapPath "/var/lib/kubelet/pods/c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10/volumeDevices/kubernetes.io~gce-pd"
2021-02-25T15:17:18+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: E0225 15:17:18.000488    2126 operation_generator.go:1073] MapVolume.NodeExpandVolume failed with MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume get PVC failed : persistentvolumeclaims "test-c3406d09-3573-418e-bd71-72a874e5d855-data1" is forbidden: User "system:node:gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12" cannot get resource "persistentvolumeclaims" in API group "" in the namespace "test": no relationship found between node "gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12" and this object
2021-02-25T15:17:18+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: E0225 15:17:18.000614    2126 nestedpendingoperations.go:301] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26 podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2021-02-25 15:17:18.500563592 +0000 UTC m=+83924.410980106 (durationBeforeRetry 500ms). Error: "MapVolume.MarkVolumeAsMounted failed while expanding volume for volume \"pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\" (UniqueName: \"kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\") pod \"test-c3406d09-3573-418e-bd71-72a874e5d855-7d4cc6b88b-tlkh6\" (UID: \"c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10\") : MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume get PVC failed : persistentvolumeclaims \"test-c3406d09-3573-418e-bd71-72a874e5d855-data1\" is forbidden: User \"system:node:gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12\" cannot get resource \"persistentvolumeclaims\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"test\": no relationship found between node \"gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12\" and this object"
```
Due to the failure above, kubelet doesn't update the actual state of the world:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2695ef3f1b0e2fc51ffb1bcb8491a4165587a089/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L1155

Now, if for some reason the deployment pod gets deleted, reconciler would try unmounting the volumes and then unmounting/detaching devices:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/445cb0609d2cffbfea4bd67a50f90f3655704ad1/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go#L163

Given the actual state of the world wasn't updated during mount, reconciler skips unmounting the volume and proceeds with unmounting/detaching the device. However, this step fails because kubelet thinks some other pod is using this volume when in fact the only pod that is using the volume is the one being deleted:
```

2021-02-25T15:17:18+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: E0225 15:17:18.051430    2126 nestedpendingoperations.go:301] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26 podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2021-02-25 15:17:18.551389407 +0000 UTC m=+83924.461805897 (durationBeforeRetry 500ms). Error: "UnmapDevice failed for volume \"pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\" (UniqueName: \"kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\") on node \"gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12\" : The device \"/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/gce-pd/volumeDevices/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\" is still referenced from other Pods [/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/gce-pd/volumeDevices/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26/c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10]"
2021-02-25T15:17:18+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:18.552560    2126 reconciler.go:312] operationExecutor.UnmountDevice started for volume "pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26") on node "gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12"
2021-02-25T15:17:18+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: E0225 15:17:18.552768    2126 nestedpendingoperations.go:301] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26 podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2021-02-25 15:17:19.55273784 +0000 UTC m=+83925.463154306 (durationBeforeRetry 1s). Error: "UnmapDevice failed for volume \"pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\" (UniqueName: \"kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\") on node \"gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12\" : The device \"/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/gce-pd/volumeDevices/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26\" is still referenced from other Pods [/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/gce-pd/volumeDevices/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26/c2b710b3-2dc2-40ce-9867-7e77f6a6cb10]"
2021-02-25T15:17:19+0000 gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12 kubelet[2126]: I0225 15:17:19.555836    2126 reconciler.go:312] operationExecutor.UnmountDevice started for volume "pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/gce-pd/gke-test-cluste-pvc-e1ea45c4-8423-4eeb-b952-f024a04d8f26") on node "gke-test-clus-n1-standard-4-po-b3a760df-5n12"
```
Failed detaches go on for 6 minutes until the attach-detach controller forcibly detaches the volume. During this interval, a new pod can't start on a new node and hence suffers from a significant downtime.

#### What you expected to happen:

Broadly speaking, kubelet should tolerate brief API server outages or other intermittent failures in face of random events like pod deletions. More specifically, the volume should get detached immediately when the pod that's triggering the detach is the only consumer of the volume.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Rapid creation and deletion of a pod belonging to a deployment coupled with an API server outage (and/or node authorization issue) is how the issue was encountered.

comments:
Any reason we don't call `actualStateOfWorld.MarkVolumeAsMounted(markVolumeOpts)` before `og.nodeExpandVolume(volumeToMount, actualStateOfWorld, resizeOptions)`? The alternative would be to not return error when `nodeExpandVolume` fails, assuming resize would be retried later:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2695ef3f1b0e2fc51ffb1bcb8491a4165587a089/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L1152

I'm happy to create a PR with the fix based on the discussion here. Thanks!

I think we should copy the behavior of `GenerateMountVolumeFunc`. The volume is mounted, then it's [marked as mounted](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2695ef3f1b0e2fc51ffb1bcb8491a4165587a089/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L619), then resize is attempted and only if it fails, the volume is marked as *uncertain*. Therefore, kubelet will go through unmounting the volume to resolve the uncertain state.

I looked at  the sources, `GenerateMapVolumeFunc` *should* mark volumes as uncertain on error, especially after `MapVolume.MapPodDevice succeeded for volume` in logs. Even in 1.18:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e991415386e4cf155a24b1da15becaa390438d8/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L1002-L1009

Either it does not work as expected or it's something else

Thanks @kangarlou for bringing it up. It seems an issue in both MapVolume and MountVolume case. Should put MarkVolumeMounted before resize operation.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e991415386e4cf155a24b1da15becaa390438d8/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L629-L677

review_comments: Why are we calling MarkVolumeMountAsUncertain here, but in the CustomBlockMapper case above, we markVolumeErrorState? Should't we be consistent in the two cases?

I think it is mostly fine because `Setup` functions for CSI driver has been changed to return appropriate errors if operation finished with a final error or in-progress-uncertain error. So `makeVolumeErrorState` can take all of that into account.

Volume expansion operation functions only return final errors and hence can't use `markVolumeErrorState` function.
